entries.title: Overview drag-and-drop & navigation polish
changes: Habits street: the buildings look more lived-in, with soot and rain streaks down the walls, stone corner blocks on brick floors and iron fire escapes on some buildings.
Cat tab: the furniture's 3D sides and tops now fade in and out smoothly as the camera pans, instead of jumping between a few fixed pictures; a still camera shows the same room as before.
Cat tab: choosing a cat (tap it in the room, or switch cats on the Together card) now pans the camera to that cat and keeps following it, also in the full-screen room.

Cat tab: the room now always has a gentle 3D view angle, so the furniture shows its sides and near and far layers are offset even when nothing moves; it also keeps the strongest 3D level on phones that run the screen slower than their top refresh rate.

Your cat's coat now holds steady while it sits, loafs or sleeps: the little shading speckles no longer flip between frames, which was most noticeable on black cats. Kitten faces also get a complete outline.

Cat tab: a cat sitting still, such as on the cat tree, now keeps one head pose for several seconds instead of changing it about three times a second, so it no longer looks restless; blinking and breathing are unchanged.

Native Cat (beta, Settings > Appearance): the Cat tab now has a Cattery, a Breeding lab, adopting a second cat and an In memory list. Pick a mother and a father, see the page's forecast, then keep or release each kitten, bring one home, rename or release a cattery cat (with a confirmation).

Native Cat (beta): the Cat tab now opens when you have no cat yet, so you can adopt your first kitten there, and after a cat has passed, where it shows the In memory page with Open the door again. The Breeding lab's Another stray button is now on the lab itself, for when you have no mother or no father to pair.

Cattery and Breeding lab: Another stray now arrives as a grown cat, as its button says, instead of a newborn, so it can be paired with at once. After you adopt a kitten, the next time the adoption card opens it offers a fresh litter.
Native Cat (beta): if the phone's confirmation of a saved world is lost on the way, the Cat tab now catches up with what was saved and carries on instead of retrying the same save.

Native Cat (beta): your native cats now tell the album and the Likes what they did while you watched. Hours spent in a place and time playing alone with a toy now make a favourite place and toy, and their first zoomies become an album moment.

Cat tab: three new rooms for the cats to explore, placed beside the house and opening as your cats grow closer to you: the Sunroom (bond Curious), the Study (Friendly) and the Bathroom (Fond), each with simple placeholder art for now. Once a room opens the cats walk there, rest on its floor and climb its furniture (the Sunroom's window bench, the Study's desk and tall shelf, the Bathroom's tub and sink), and the camera follows them; a room that has just opened shows from the next time the app starts, and the app now remembers which rooms are open.

New Habits tab (Android app): build habits as stacks. Each foundation, something you already do (after coffee, at lights out), is a building on one street, and each habit stacked on it is a floor whose windows light up, with the odd person at work inside, when you do it; scroll along the street, tap a floor to tune it, and zoom out to the whole street with a 12-week time-lapse. Floors go from steel and glass to brick, stone and gold trim as a habit sets, shrink to two minutes on a rough day and crack when you miss, a habit you are breaking is a run-down building that loses a floor each clean day, and the city around it lives, with twinkling stars, planes and birds. As you type a foundation or a habit, suggestions appear under the field; picking a habit fills in its two-minute, normal and stretch versions. Habits are kept on your phone in their own file and are included in Android device backup; they are not yet part of the backup file you export from Settings.

Habits: sheets such as New habit now rise from the bottom above the bottom bar and stay in view above the keyboard with the field and suggestions, and the top bar no longer disappears after scrolling inside a sheet.

Habits: the building in front now keeps its ground floor, sign and awning clear of the Rough day switch and the big button, also at large text sizes, and a tall building tilts only as far as that allows. The whole-street view has a slimmer time-lapse card, so the buildings are bigger, and a + Foundation button beside Building.

Habits: the top bar now sits on the app's own background with the street starting under it, and the sky is nicer to look at: softly lit painted clouds that glow peach at dusk and silver at night, a refined blimp, plane and gulls, fuller layered trees that sway, with better lamps, windows that glow, sun, moon and stars. Each floor's label is now frosted glass, and the windows now look like real rooms at night: each lit window is a furnished room (desk, shelves, lamp, curtains, plants, cats on the sills), and only a few people are visible at a time, each warm back-lit figure reading, typing, cooking, stretching, running, playing guitar or the like for a while before leaving, so you catch life in a window every now and then rather than in all of them; a new floor gets a short cheer of a few people appearing, someone walks along a floor now and then, and the lobby has a receptionist and an occasional visitor. Smoother walking: everyone who walks, in the lobby, along a floor or past a window, now takes a proper stride with swinging arms, and the lobby visitor eases into a walk, stops, turns to look at the street and turns back.

Habits: the street now has real light and shadow. The sun (and at night the moon) stands where the sky shows it, and every building, tree, lamp and bench throws a true shadow onto the pavement that leans with the hour: long and to the right in the morning, short at noon, long and to the left in the evening, with sunlight falling through the gaps between buildings. Tree shadows sway with the trees, clouds drift their shadows across the street by day, and at night the lobby windows light the pavement and the visitor's shadow slides across it as they walk past the glass.
Habits: a failing light on a missed floor now dims and comes back smoothly now and then, instead of strobing on and off.

Habits: the light now behaves as if it is in the scene. Shadows fan out from where the sun (or moon) stands and swing as you scroll the street under it; each building is lit from the side facing the sun, with its shading sliding across as you pan and its side face lighting up when the sun is on that side; the sun's glint travels across the window glass as you move; tree shadows are sharp at the trunk and soft at the crown; and at night the street lamps throw warm pools of light on the walls beside them.

Habits: the sky's small details are now painted art. The sun has a real disc with a bright core and soft limb, a corona of streamers, slow rays and a wide glow, and turns deep orange at dusk; the moon shows its seas and ray craters and its actual phase for today's date, with a soft terminator and faint earthshine on the dark side.

Habits: the airplane is a proper airliner (shaded fuselage, engines, windows, lights and a strobe at night) with a contrail that spreads and breaks up behind it; the blimp is repainted with a lit panel at night; the birds come in near and far sizes with bodies and bending wings, each on its own beat, one gliding now and then.

Habits: the car on the far road is now a tiny painted vehicle (four kinds, sometimes two in a row) with headlight beams and road reflections at night; shooting stars are real meteors with a glowing head, a tapering streak, shed sparkles and a train that lingers and fades, and rarely a brighter fireball.

Habits: people walk like people now. Each person has their own gait (stride, cadence, arm swing, bob, posture, and the odd slight limp), no two steps are the same (the timing drifts a little, with an occasional hesitation), and someone standing shifts their weight and checks a watch instead of freezing. Feet still never slide.

Habits: the street has weather, seeded from the date so each day is its own: clear, overcast (flat grey light, no shadows to speak of), rain with slanted streaks, splashes and drips off the awnings, a wet pavement that mirrors the lit shopfronts, signs and lamps with puddles rippling in the rain and drying over a couple of hours, and misty early mornings over the far city.

Habits: the street follows the seasons from today's date. Trees turn amber and red in autumn and drop leaves that tumble down and slide along the pavement, stand bare with snow on their branches in winter (with snowfall on some days and snow lying on sills, awnings, roofs, benches, lamps and the kerb), come back thin and light in spring with some in pink or white blossom, and fill out for summer.
Habits: when the sun is in the picture by day there is a soft camera-style lens flare whose ghosts drift across the picture as you pan, and which fades when a building hides the sun.

Habits: the street has life on it. Every minute or so someone walks the length of the pavement (a plain walker, a dog walker whose dog trots ahead and stops to sniff, a cyclist, or two people side by side), each with their own clothes, bag and walk, their own uneven steps, a shadow that leans with the sun by day and, at night, swings from behind them to ahead of them as they pass under each street lamp, warming in its light.

Habits: a car passes on the near road now and then; at night its headlights throw a cone and a pool ahead, its tail lights glow, and as it goes by its light sweeps across the building fronts and makes the lamp posts' and trees' shadows swing across the walls.

Habits: the buildings turn with the camera as the street scrolls. A building left of the middle of the screen shows its right side, one right of the middle shows its left, and the side grows as it moves toward the edge, so the street reads as real 3D when you pan.
Habits: by day the people in the windows are flat dark shapes behind the glass, without the warm glow round them that belongs to a lit room at night; the two looks cross-fade through dusk.

Habits: the birds fly with depth now. A flock comes in large from one side, banks, and flies away into the distance, shrinking, sinking toward the far rooftops and fading into the haze; sometimes one arrives out of the distance instead.

Habits: dusk happens the way it does outside. The street lamps come on first in a run along the street, then the shops and signs, then the homes one by one over the hour (a few late), and off in reverse at dawn; the walls go golden on the sun side in the last hour of light and the whole street turns cool blue in the half hour after sunset before the lamps take over.

Habits: small signs of life: a few windows flicker with TV light late in the evening, steam rises from rooftop vents, pigeons peck on cornices and by the park and scatter when someone walks past, the flag moves with the same wind as the trees, and rain leaves faint stains under the windows of stone and clay buildings.

Habits: the street has depth of field. The far city is softly out of focus and hazy with distance, with real rooflines (water tanks, parapets, a crane, a spire, a dome) and lit windows; a few near things (a railing and bollards along the bottom, a post at the side, now and then a hanging branch at a top corner) slide faster than the street as you scroll, like a camera moving down a real street.

Habits: the rooms behind the windows are real interiors now: textured walls, floors in perspective with rugs, shaded furniture and small props (books, mugs, pictures, a clock, plants), each room's own lamp lighting it and the monitor or TV casting cool light on whoever is there, sunlight falling in by day, more kinds of curtains and blinds, and new things to do (watching TV, a yoga pose, a child playing, two people talking at a table). Fifteen kinds of room in three variants each, and no two neighbouring windows alike.

Habits: the buildings are real facades now. Clay floors are laid in brick with mortar joints and the odd burnt or chipped brick, stone floors in ashlar blocks with keystones over the windows, gold floors in polished panels; every window has a frame, a sill with its shadow line and a lintel; there are string courses between floors, cornices with brackets, drainpipes, now and then an air-conditioner or a balcony, and more on the roofs (vent stacks, skylights, dishes, railings). Run-down storeys show flaking render, spray tags and a hanging gutter. The lobby has a plinth, a mullioned shopfront, a panelled door with a brass handle, a framed sign with a tube that lights at dusk and a cloth awning with a valance; the reward sign stands in a steel frame with lamps along the top.

Habits: fixes from testing: the clouds stay put when you scroll between buildings instead of jumping up or down; people walking on the street look like people in daylight (cool, natural tones) instead of having a yellow glow, and only take the warm lamp light at night; the dark smudge that sometimes appeared in a top corner (a blurred hanging branch) is gone.

Habits: a new sun and moon. By day the sun is light rather than a ball: a blown-out white centre blooming through gold into a wide glow that brightens the sky around it, with a few faint slow rays and no outline. Low in the sky it becomes a large, soft, slightly flattened orange disc with a warm glow spreading along the horizon, then fades into the haze at sunset as the moon fades in. Under overcast it is a pale bright patch behind the cloud.

Habits: the moon is a real moon: its seas in their true places, bright highlands, Tycho's rays across the south, fine craters and relief along the shadow's edge. It shows tonight's actual phase with the lit side always full bright and, on a thin crescent, the rest of the disc just faintly visible by earthshine; its glow grows as it fills. The airplane flies a little further off now (drawn smaller).
Habits: people on the street no longer glow orange at night either: they are dark, natural figures against the lit street, with only a faint warm edge where a lamp catches them.

Habits: the cyclist pedals smoothly (twice the drawn crank positions, blended) and their bicycle's wheels sit where they belong at each end of the frame; people seen through the upper windows are dark, natural figures at night too, with the warm look kept only for the lit shopfront on the ground floor.

Habits: the buildings have depth and real light. Windows are set into the walls with lit and shaded sides that turn with the sun, ledges and cornices cast shadows, every pane reflects the sky (and the far city by day), glass floors are a real curtain wall, and at night the walls go dark and are lit by their own windows, the sign, the lamps by the door and the street lamps. The ground floor has a granite front, a recessed shopfront, a proper entrance with a step and a glowing transom, and an awning that throws its shadow.

Habits (developer mode): a row of chips under the street sets the hour it is drawn at: Real, Day, Dusk or Night, so the dusk sequence, the lamps and the night can be checked at any time of day. It is remembered only until the app is closed.
The bottom bar now keeps the tab you are on and the tabs either side of it in view as you swipe along it, so the previous and next tab are never cut off at the edge.

Your cats now get about: they explore every perch, the window and the rugs, play and race round the house (kittens most), keep each other company, and rest in short, varied breaks instead of lying around. They still sleep at night, when tired and after a meal.
Settings > Data & advanced > Food database now has a Download button that fetches the USDA branded foods from GitHub (about 18 MB) and imports them, so you no longer need to pick a file.
Life Director: a long session name in the middle of the dial now wraps inside the ring instead of running past it.
Life Director: workout-plan sessions with an "&" in their name (like Active Mobility & Structural Recovery) now show a plain "&" instead of "&".
Life Director: a work shift or sleep that crosses midnight now draws as one solid arc on the dial, with no thin gap at midnight.
Returning to today now winds farther and takes longer based on how many days you travelled. A year away has a much longer rewind than a week away.
The winding date count, spring settle, and activity-ring reveal stay connected throughout the return.
Overview cards now reveal their destination with a smooth expanding transition from the tap, while the shared bars stay in place.
Press and hold an Overview card, then drag it to rearrange your dashboard. Cards lift, neighbors slide aside, and the layout saves when you drop.
The Edit button still manages hidden cards. Dragging near the screen edges scrolls the dashboard.
Life Director activity centers use compact, non-scrolling summaries and keep the main action visible. Dragging inside the center no longer scrolls the dashboard or top bar.

Hold a time on the Life Director’s outer track to schedule a pinned activity. The form starts at that date and time; moving your finger still rotates the calendar. Requires an already planned day and a free time slot.

Native Cat (beta): Play opens a toy tray right on the Cat tab. Pick a toy and a cat that feels like it comes to pick it up, carry it, toss it and chase it; a sleepy or hungry cat tells you why it won’t.
Native Cat (beta): two cats no longer lie on top of each other in one bed or stay in bed for hours, and after a meal a rested cat gets up and about instead of going straight back to sleep.
Native Cat (beta): the cats no longer rest hidden behind the sofa; resting spots by the sofa keep them in view.

Native Cat (beta): two cats now live together. They touch noses (and, while they are still strangers, hiss), chase each other, groom each other, curl up together for a nap and settle standoffs over a perch; a kitten follows the grown cat about. The Together card counts what they did, with the last moment and the pecking order, and “While you were away” mentions what they shared.
Native Cat (beta): the pale outline around the cats in the Overview card and the Cat tab is gone.
Native Cat (beta): a resting cat no longer shimmers. Its breathing is now a clean one-pixel lift, so the coat stays steady instead of popping and flickering.
Native Cat (beta): a sitting or sleeping cat’s tail no longer bulges below it for a moment; the tail stays resting on the floor in every frame.
Scrubbing along the bottom bar now keeps going when your finger passes over or ends on Quest. A scrub that starts on Quest still uses the older scrubber until Quest is native.
Native Cat (beta): cats now turn round step by step, through a three-quarter and a front view, instead of just flipping. It takes about a third of a second.

Native Cat (beta): cats no longer walk through the sofa. A cat crossing the living room goes round the sofa's front instead of sinking into its arm, and a cat on the cat tree's middle platform lies low instead of sitting with its head in the top one.

Native Cat (beta): when you feed the cats they go and eat again. Two cats fed together walk side by side to their bowls instead of sending each other away, a cat fed while jumping onto the sofa or a perch comes down to its bowl instead of eating up there, and a meal served from the Cat page, the voice or a link reaches the cats on the Overview card too.
Native Cat (beta): cats no longer poke through the cat tree. A cat scratches the post from in front of the tree, and one passing under its platform is drawn in front of it.
Developer: with developer mode on (Settings), the native Cat tab has a Demo parkour button that sends one cat on a climbing tour of the room; it changes nothing in your save.

Native economy check (beta): a new switch in Settings, Data & advanced, off by default. When it is on, the phone works out every XP and Sparks change the app makes itself (Logs, rewards, the shop, rest days, settings, quests, the Daily Hand, Health sync and the new day's decay) and only counts whether it got the same answer. It never saves or shows its own numbers, and nothing leaves the phone.

Native economy check (beta): the card under the switch says what the check is doing in plain words (checking, how many actions and how many came out different, paused for Battery Saver or an app update, or stopped and why) and when the last difference was. You don't need to do anything but use the app.

Native economy check (beta): Copy report puts a short summary on the clipboard to paste to the assistant (counts and field names only, never your activity names, notes or journal); Clear starts the counts again after asking; Save case… can save one difference in full to a file you choose, after a warning that the file holds your real data.

Native Life Director check (beta): a new switch in Settings, Data & advanced, under the economy check, off by default. When it is on, the phone also works out Life Director's plans, its week and what it saves, and only counts whether it got the same answer. It never saves or shows its own results, and nothing leaves the phone. Copy report gives a short summary to paste to the assistant (counts and field names only, never your goals or sessions).

Habits: softer, more natural light. Street lamps now glow in the air and fade onto the pavement with no visible beam edges, shop windows spill a soft-edged pool of light that spreads and fades, and building shadows by day have soft edges that blur more the further they fall, softer still on hazy or cloudy days. People walking under a street lamp at night are now lit by it the way real light falls: brightest on their head, shoulders and the side facing the lamp, fading down to their feet, and growing as they walk in under the lamp and fading as they walk on. Air conditioners, balconies and boarded windows now darken at night like the walls around them.

Habits: smoother, more natural walking, with twice as many poses in each step for the people on the street. The swinging leg now folds at the knee early and reaches out long to the heel, arms swing like pendulums (lingering at each end, quicker through the middle) with the forearms trailing, heads stay level instead of rocking with the body, and each kind of walker on the street has its own arm swing, bounce, posture and hip and shoulder movement.

Habits: the sun and moon now hide behind thick clouds instead of shining through them, a passing cloud's thin edges light up with a silver lining, the sun's rays fan out through the gaps when it is partly hidden, and thin cloud over the moon spreads its light into a soft corona; and the windows of a missed floor stay dark instead of flickering on and off.

Habits: the people on the street are now shown in their own colours instead of dark silhouettes: skin tones, hair, coats, jeans, skirts, shoes and bags, with light and shade, a face in profile and details like belts, buttons and collars; at night they are dimmer and cooler but still in colour. The cyclist has a detailed bicycle (chain and chainring, pedals, saddle, mudguards, lamps that light at night), a soft shadow under the wheels, a helmet, and pedals twice as smoothly, the hips, knees and ankles moving with each stroke. Planes now fly further off, smaller and slower across the sky.

Habits: a richer sky. By day it is deep blue overhead and hazy near the horizon; at sunrise and sunset a warm glow sits under the sun with rose and violet above it, and clouds glow gold and coral underneath; at night the sky is near-black overhead with the city's glow at the horizon, stars in their own colours, and on dark clear nights a faint Milky Way, while night clouds are dark with moonlit edges.

Habits: the street lamps, trees and benches now look solid instead of flat. Lamp posts are round and lit on the sun's side, standing on a stepped base with a domed hood; benches show their seat and the thickness of their ends; trees have a rounded crown that is darker on the far side and underneath. As you scroll, they turn with the view like the buildings do, slide a touch faster than the buildings behind them, and a tree's back leaves shift against its front ones.

Habits: a missed floor now wears down the way a real building does instead of showing a scribbled crack. Missed once, a fine crack runs along the brickwork from a window and one pane cracks; twice, the crack widens, a few bricks come away, rust runs down and a broken window is taped across; three times or more, a window is boarded up with a notice on it and rubble lies below. The yellow warning triangle is gone, and a habit you pick back up has its crack filled with gold mortar.

entries.title: Life Director polish & update history
changes: Read what changed in Settings → Phone & sync → App updates → What’s new.
Unplanned dates show your sleep and work hours, with a message that the day hasn’t been planned yet.
Double-tap an empty corner outside the Life Director dial to return to today with a winding animation.
The date fades into your current activity while its colored ring draws around the dial center.
Dial rotation keeps following your thumb after it drifts away from the outer rim.
Switch Life Director sections by tapping their buttons; accidental sideways swipes no longer change sections.
